nodes.label: Ad Placement Targeting Widening (sql/078)
nodes.rationale: ADR-0044 Fase 2 step 1: widen awcms_news_portal_ad_placements with target_type/target_id BEFORE deleting the legacy free-URL ad system, because deleting first would silently destroy per-post/per-page targeting with no error. Migration 078 deliberately moves no data and drops no table.

nodes.label: placement_key is SLOT, target_type/target_id is SCOPE
nodes.rationale: placement_key answers WHERE on the page, target_type/target_id answers WHICH page. The two axes are orthogonal and must not be collapsed.
nodes.norm_label: placement_key is slot, target_type/target_id is scope

nodes.label: Union render: page-targeted ads merged with global ads
nodes.rationale: Deliberate fix over the legacy system, which matched exactly one scope and left merging to the caller.
nodes.norm_label: union render: page-targeted ads merged with global ads

nodes.label: Polymorphic target_id without foreign key
nodes.rationale: target_id spans post/page/widget so no FK can reach it. Existence is checked at write time; a target deleted LATER is never an error, the row simply stops matching. Paired rule (target_id required for targeted types, forbidden for global) is a DB CHECK, not just a validator, and is tested by INSERT as the admin role because that writer is unreachable by application-level rules.

nodes.label: blog:ads:ingest job
nodes.rationale: ADR-0044 Fase 2 step 2: moves free-URL ads into the media-backed system and reports every row it cannot move. --apply requires --placement-key because the legacy system had no slot concept and nothing in the old data says which of the twelve slots applies; the job refuses to guess. Writes no SQL itself: all statements live in application/legacy-ad-ingest-directory.ts, owned by the table-owning module.

nodes.label: Preview-by-default (--apply is opt-in)
nodes.rationale: Inverted from other scheduled jobs that use --dry-run as opt-in. Those run unattended and their normal mode is to work; here the expensive mistake is not 'forgot to preview' but 'previewed, then never read the residue' by an operator about to drop the source table.

nodes.label: Refusal to fetch external URLs during ingest
nodes.rationale: Fetching remote URLs server-side is an SSRF primitive, and the worst place to build one is a run-once data migration script executed under time pressure by an operator watching row counts instead of egress. The repo already settled this stance on the OIDC discovery path (ADR-0031). Second rejected shortcut: registering bucket objects with no registry row, which would print 'verified' for bytes never fetched, sniffed, or size-bounded; awcms_worker is not even granted the INSERT that would allow it (sql/079).
nodes.norm_label: refusal to fetch external urls during ingest

nodes.label: source_legacy_ad_id partial unique index with NULLS NOT DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: Both halves are load-bearing: without NULLS NOT DISTINCT a second run duplicates every global ad; without the partial predicate the index rejects ordinary editorial work. Both sides proven by mutation against real PostgreSQL 16.
nodes.norm_label: source_legacy_ad_id partial unique index with nulls not distinct

nodes.label: NEWS_MEDIA_R2_* absent from .env.example
nodes.rationale: Found in passing: operators copying .env.example had no way to discover the five required media_library variables.

nodes.label: 410 ENDPOINT_RETIRED on POST/PATCH /api/v1/blog/ads
nodes.rationale: Answers without auth and without touching the database. Both stored free-text imageUrl rendered straight into a public — the managed-media bypass ADR-0036 closed, open as long as any route can write it. Closing POST alone is insufficient: PATCH can rewrite imageUrl on an existing ad, the same bypass through a quieter route that produces no new row for anyone to notice. GET and DELETE deliberately survive so an operator working the residue report can read and retire rows.

nodes.label: blog:ads:drop-readiness gate
nodes.rationale: Answers 'may the two legacy tables be dropped now?' from data and exits non-zero while the answer is no. The drop migration is irreversible and carries live site ads; every safeguard in the epic is decoration if the last step is taken on someone's memory of having run ingest. A legacy ad counts as decided if a successor row names it via source_legacy_ad_id OR it is soft-deleted. No override flag — a gate that can be told to pass is a gate nobody needs to satisfy.

nodes.label: RLS silently doing what an explicit predicate claims
nodes.rationale: Removing the p.tenant_id = a.tenant_id predicate from the readiness query passed all seven tests because RLS quietly did the same job. Two mechanisms were claimed and a test that cannot tell them apart only proves at least one exists. The eighth test runs the same assessment as an admin role that bypasses RLS entirely, so the predicate is the only barrier — and the mutation is now red.
nodes.norm_label: rls silently doing what an explicit predicate claims

nodes.label: CONTENT_BLOCK_TYPES runtime vocabulary
nodes.rationale: The content_json block vocabulary as a RUNTIME value, unified with the ContentBlock union via mutually-assignable assertions. Adding a variant to the union without adding it to the constant (or vice versa) reddens typecheck rather than a test someone might not run. Proven both directions.

nodes.label: BlogContentBlock / BlogContentJson OpenAPI schema
nodes.rationale: oneOf over six full variants, referenced from ALL FIVE contentJson occurrences (previously four said only type: object). The two most guessable shapes carry explicit notes: ordering is a FIELD on list (there is no ordered_list type), and gallery/video_news have no text field.

nodes.label: Prose-only vocabulary gets re-derived, and re-derivation is where it breaks
nodes.rationale: awcms-astro re-derived the vocabulary by reading and got three things wrong at once: invented an ordered_list type that does not exist, and dropped gallery and video_news because neither has a text field while its fallback rendered text. Nothing failed anywhere — numbered lists came out bulleted and media sections vanished from live pages.
nodes.norm_label: prose-only vocabulary gets re-derived, and re-derivation is where it breaks

nodes.label: tests/content-block-contract.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Pins the OpenAPI contract and the renderer switch to the same constant, asserts every type renders something non-empty, and that no variant emits raw HTML. Mutation-tested: contract naming a different type (1 red), one contentJson reverted to plain type: object (1 red), renderer dropping gallery (2 red).

nodes.label: Graphify tracked graph artifact refresh
nodes.rationale: Regeneration spans 1,435 files (from 1,412), 23,752 edges (from 21,477), 99% EXTRACTED (from 98%), produced entirely from cache with 0 input tokens.

nodes.label: Untracking .graphify_labels.json
nodes.rationale: It is an intermediate build artifact the skill's cleanup step deletes at the end of every run, so a tracked copy can only be the residue of an interrupted run — the same reason .graphify_analysis.json was ignored earlier. Its community labels are already rendered into GRAPH_REPORT.md and derived from the tracked graph.json.

nodes.label: ADR-0044: merge news_portal into blog_content
nodes.rationale: news_portal had stopped carrying its own weight: 11 files against 59, 3 tables against 18, zero capabilities provided, zero public routes, and a MANDATORY consumer of blog_content's public_content — every homepage section type was built on that module's data. A capability seam exists to describe two modules that could plausibly change independently; these two could not. Moves 8 domain/application files into src/modules/blog-content/.

nodes.label: Two ad systems, one weakening the other's security control
nodes.rationale: awcms_blog_ads.image_url accepts any URL while awcms_news_portal_ad_placements.media_object_id is an FK to a verified media object. While both live, a tenant can switch on managed-media enforcement (ADR-0036) and still publish arbitrary remote images through the other door.
nodes.norm_label: two ad systems, one weakening the other's security control

nodes.label: Union, not subtraction
nodes.rationale: The two ad systems are not one feature with two spellings: the old one has post/page targeting the new lacks; the new one has 12 placement slots, 4 rotation modes and priority the old lacks. Replacing either with the other would silently delete capability — which is why this change is written as a UNION and why unifying the ad tables is done separately, after the destination table is widened first.

nodes.label: Preserve awcms_news_portal_* table names and API paths
nodes.rationale: Follows the ADR-0036 precedent that moved the media registry without renaming awcms_news_media_objects. A rename eats every FK, policy, index and consumer while buying nothing the descriptor and inventory do not already record. Table names are therefore no longer a hint about module ownership.
nodes.norm_label: preserve awcms_news_portal_* table names and api paths

nodes.label: sql/076 permission repoint: insert, move grants, then delete
nodes.rationale: The ordering IS the point: deleting first would revoke the capability from every tenant that held it, with all gates still green.
nodes.norm_label: sql/076 permission repoint: insert, move grants, then delete

nodes.label: DROP awcms_news_portal_tenant_state (sql/077)
nodes.rationale: Its writer was never ported, so the table was inert; a FORCE-RLS table with no owner and no writer is a false claim standing in front of every inventory gate.

nodes.label: tests/news-portal-merge.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Guards the 'union, not subtraction' promise by pinning each surviving feature to something observable: a registry entry, a declared permission, a claimed route prefix, a file on disk, or the statement order in its migration.

nodes.label: AWCMS Project Skills catalog
nodes.rationale: Project-level Claude Code skills encoding docs/awcms standards so coding agents apply them consistently. Adapted from ahliweb/awcms-mini and now awcms-micro (ADR-0035 absorption). Correction: the repo has 20 active modules and sql/001-sql/079, not the 'four modules, Sprint 1-2 foundation' earlier versions claimed.

nodes.label: Skill usage map (mermaid flowchart)
nodes.rationale: Directed graph from awcms-implement-issue (orchestrator) into module/migration/endpoint/event/testing skills, then into review, security, preflight, deploy, release.

nodes.label: Verify package.json scripts before running a skill's commands
nodes.rationale: 75 scripts exist now, including ones previously marked absent. Genuinely absent: repo:inventory:* (modules:composition:inventory:* is a different scope), i18n:*, and extension:check — the last DELETED by ADR-0034, not pending, so it must not be referenced. The list moves every time a module lands.
nodes.norm_label: verify package.json scripts before running a skill's commands

nodes.label: AWCMS subagents (coder, reviewer, security-auditor)
nodes.rationale: Usage pattern: awcms-coder implements an issue, awcms-reviewer reviews it, sensitive modules are audited by awcms-security-auditor (both reviewers read-only).

nodes.label: blog_content module
nodes.rationale: First domain module registered directly in the base repo (epic #536). Ported in PR #214: src/modules/blog-content, migrations sql/035-sql/040, 15 awcms_blog_* tables all FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Since ADR-0044 (PR #300) it ABSORBS all of news_portal. Port delta vs the mini spec: path-based public routes /blog/{tenantCode} (ADR-0009) rather than host-resolved /news/**, and no blog admin UI port for src/pages/admin/blog.

nodes.label: evaluateContentUpdateAccess generic ABAC ownership override
nodes.rationale: One generic function used by posts AND pages (an author may edit their own unpublished content without the update permission); new resources call it rather than copying evaluatePostUpdateAccess/evaluatePageUpdateAccess. Revision restore deliberately has NO such override — blog_content.revisions.restore is required explicitly even for the post's own author.

nodes.label: Two different public visibility predicates (listing vs detail)
nodes.rationale: Listing (index/category/tag/search/feed/sitemap) uses strict visibility = 'public'; detail uses visibility IN ('public','unlisted') so unlisted is reachable by direct link but never listed. private is never public in either context. Do not unify them.
nodes.norm_label: two different public visibility predicates (listing vs detail)

nodes.label: Revisions are append-only (rule 3)
nodes.rationale: awcms_blog_revisions rows are never UPDATEd or DELETEd. 'Restore revision' writes the old content back onto the live post then inserts a NEW revision recording the restored state. A revision is only created when a PATCH touches title/contentJson/contentText (isSignificantContentChange) — cosmetic fields do not trigger one.

nodes.label: Rule 21: enqueue edge purge inside the content transaction
nodes.rationale: enqueueModuleContentPurge(tx, tenantId, 'blog_content', reason) must run in the SAME transaction as the change — the outbox pattern (ADR-0006): a rolled-back publish leaves no stray purge and a committed publish cannot lose its purge. Scope is MODULE, not resource: cached responses are tagged with tenant/surface/module keys only, so a resource-scoped ban matches nothing while the queue reports success. The source-level call-count test locks three files, so a fourth mutation handler without an enqueue reddens no handler test but serves stale pages until TTL.
nodes.norm_label: rule 21: enqueue edge purge inside the content transaction

nodes.label: Rule 18: no base media library (pre-ADR-0036 rule)
nodes.rationale: Do not invent new media tables/endpoints for gallery/attachment needs; add a block type to the rendering whitelist or store a loose UUID/URL. Since #636, when full-online R2-only mode is active for a tenant, those loose references MUST resolve to a safe registry row — still not a new media library inside blog_content, only validation of a reference into another module's registry.
nodes.norm_label: rule 18: no base media library (pre-adr-0036 rule)

nodes.label: blog_content as cross-module descriptor contributor (seo_facts, searchSources)
nodes.rationale: module.ts provides capability seo_facts (consumed by seo_distribution) and declares searchSources read by site_search via listModules(). Both are PURE DATA — declarative table/column names and publication filters, no cross imports. Renaming a post table/column, changing publication status, or changing the public URL template requires updating the descriptor or site-search:sources:check goes red and the search index lies.
nodes.norm_label: blog_content as cross-module descriptor contributor (seo_facts, searchsources)

nodes.label: Rule 7: public routes are APIRoute .ts, not .astro
nodes.rationale: So they are testable through tests/integration/harness.ts invoke()/invokeRaw() — the repo's only test pattern. invokeRaw is required for HTML/XML handlers because invoke always JSON.parses.
nodes.norm_label: rule 7: public routes are apiroute .ts, not .astro

nodes.label: media_library capability consumption (news_media retired)
nodes.rationale: Capability news_media is retired and its key deliberately NOT reused, so consumers still asking for it fail loudly instead of silently binding to a different port. Replacement is media_library with a real adapter injected at every composition root. ADR-0044 also raised media_library from optional to a REQUIRED capability for blog_content because the absorbed ad placements hold a real FK.

nodes.label: CodeQL triage process
nodes.rationale: Fetch real alerts via gh api (never from memory), read most_recent_instance.message.text rather than the generic rule text, look for the identical pattern in unflagged files as evidence of a context-dependent false positive, then fix with a minimal behavior-preserving change. Inline suppression comments were tried and proven ineffective in this repo's CI (PR #505). Official dismissal requires dismissed_reason exactly 'false positive'/'won't fix'/'used in tests' (spaces, not underscores) and a comment capped at 280 characters.

nodes.label: js/insufficient-password-hash name heuristic false positive
nodes.rationale: CodeQL flags the return value of ANY function whose name contains 'password'. Definitive proof: validateForgotPasswordInput returns an object with no password field at all. Fix that worked was renaming the functions; prevention is to avoid the substring in names whose return value is a token/identifier/DTO rather than a real password hash.

nodes.label: js/comparison-between-incompatible-types on the typeof/null idiom
nodes.rationale: typeof value === 'object' && value !== null is the standard non-null-object check, yet CodeQL calls the null comparison incompatible after narrowing. Identical code in four other files is unflagged, showing per-call-site flow analysis divergence. Fix: test value === null BEFORE the typeof narrowing; runtime behaviour is identical.

nodes.label: js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization in test fetch mocks
nodes.rationale: The rule targets production code deciding whether a URL is TRUSTED by prefix; the test mocks use the prefix to REJECT, and both sides are test-controlled. Still fixed rather than suppressed because startsWith was also accidentally looser than intended: compare new URL(url).origin exactly.

nodes.label: Official dismissal without code reformulation (alerts #16-#18)
nodes.rationale: generateOAuthState returns 256-bit CSPRNG output, not user input, and its sha256:<hex> shape matches three unflagged token files — a slow hash buys nothing against an unbrute-forceable random value. For the clear-text-logging alerts only the literal variable NAME reaches console.log; the secret value only ever appears inside boolean predicates, and removing the name would destroy the tool's usefulness to operators. Verify every path that actually reaches the sink before dismissing.

nodes.label: js/implicit-operand-conversion on a Bun.SQL tagged template
nodes.rationale: A tagged template does NOT perform implicit toString — substitutions are passed raw to the tag function and bound as real SQL parameters, so the accused conversion never happens regardless of the value being provably null. Identical patterns on the same line range and in 12+ other files are unflagged; dismissed rather than reformulated.
nodes.norm_label: js/implicit-operand-conversion on a bun.sql tagged template

nodes.label: js/trivial-conditional on a build-time extension seam (historic)
nodes.rationale: applicationModuleRegistry was always undefined in the base repo by design, so the ternary was trivial HERE but genuinely conditional once a derived repo replaced the file. Now obsolete: ADR-0034 deleted the derived pathway and the file. The general principle (an intentionally-undefined extension point in boolean context always trips this rule, and that is healthy) still holds.
nodes.norm_label: js/trivial-conditional on a build-time extension seam (historic)

nodes.label: js/trivial-conditional as a REAL dead-code bug (alert #140)
nodes.rationale: asRecord always returns a non-null object, so the ?? fallback to the first media type was dead code and error responses with only non-JSON media types were wrongly reported as not resolving to ApiError. Triage rule: when CodeQL says 'call to <fn> always evaluates to true', read <fn> — if its return type is never nullish while the call site treats it as if it could be, that is a real bug; fix it, do not dismiss.
nodes.norm_label: js/trivial-conditional as a real dead-code bug (alert #140)

nodes.label: js/unused-local-variable in tests can mark a coverage gap
nodes.rationale: Of 11 such alerts, 8 were genuine leftovers but 3 were correctly-written helpers that were never called, each pointing at a missing test path (a category_grid accept case, an R2 deletion assertion the test title promised, an untested exported function). Before deleting a binding, check whether its name matches a capability named in another test title, the file docstring, or a sibling function — then wire it to a new assertion instead.
nodes.norm_label: js/unused-local-variable in tests can mark a coverage gap

nodes.label: document_infrastructure module (NOT ported; port spec)
nodes.rationale: Lives in awcms-mini, not this repo: ls src/modules has no document-infrastructure and sql/ has no migration. Every path, table and sql/NNN in the skill is a mini artifact. An Official Optional Module: generic tenant-scoped document metadata infrastructure, opt-in per tenant. It never implements domain document schemas, never stores binary bytes in Postgres, never implements e-signature or a universal retention schedule, and never imports or writes another module's tables.

nodes.label: Concurrency-safe numbering via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: reserveNumber locks the currently-open sequence definition row (effective_to IS NULL) before reading/incrementing current_value, so concurrent callers serialize on the Postgres row lock. UNIQUE (tenant_id, sequence_id, reserved_number) is the database-level backstop. Do NOT swap to optimistic locking for performance: pessimistic serialization is deliberate because a lost update here means a duplicate or missing document number, not a stale read. Format templates are parsed by a limited hand-written token grammar, never eval or free regex.
nodes.norm_label: concurrency-safe numbering via select ... for update

nodes.label: Confidentiality-tier gating
nodes.rationale: Base read permissions only reach public/internal rows; confidential/restricted need ADDITIVE documents_confidential.read / documents_restricted.read. Rows outside the caller's clearance return results IDENTICAL to 'not found' — never confirming existence. Since #787 MUTATION endpoints also require clearance against the document's CURRENT level as a precondition, before the action-specific permission is evaluated.

nodes.label: Idempotency-hash resource binding (recurring bug class)
nodes.rationale: 11 endpoints hashed the request WITHOUT the identity path params or an explicit action literal. Because request_scope is shared across all same-type resources in a tenant, reusing an Idempotency-Key across two documents replayed the first document's response for a request meant to mutate the second. 4 of the 11 were found only by a second independent auditor re-grepping the WHOLE module — do not trust a list of suspicious-looking endpoints as complete. Index-level and pure-create endpoints were checked and are not vulnerable.

nodes.label: document_resource_relations capability port
nodes.rationale: Other modules import and call linkDocumentToResource/unlinkDocumentFromResource/listRelationsFor* in-process (the ADR-0011 pattern also used for blog_content to media_library) instead of writing awcms_document_resource_relations directly (ADR-0013 §6 no-shared-table-write). ownerModuleKey/resourceType/resourceId are OPAQUE strings here; the CALLING module is responsible for only passing ids it already validated as its own tenant's. Proven reusable across five different domain scenarios with no domain knowledge in this module.

nodes.label: awcms_document_versions is immutable and append-only
nodes.rationale: No updated_at/deleted_at columns and no UPDATE/DELETE anywhere in the module; corrections are a new version with previous_version_id pointing backwards. current_version_number on awcms_documents is a denormalized cache updated only by document-version-service.ts.

nodes.label: decideCacheability: allow-list, not deny-list
nodes.rationale: Refuses by default; a new route is not cacheable until someone declares its surface. 'Cache everything except /admin' is precisely the failure mode that makes shared caches dangerous. Also: an unresolved tenant is never cached, because an object with no tenant key is unreachable by any purge and would be stale forever.

nodes.label: Three layers of default-deny
nodes.rationale: (a) the app labels every response explicitly — Surrogate-Control or Cache-Control: private, no-store, with no silent third state; (b) VCL caches only what carries Surrogate-Control; (c) default_ttl=0. Removing one as 'redundant' removes exactly the intended redundancy. Identity cookies are matched by the awcms_ PREFIX rather than a name list so a new identity cookie cannot quietly open a hole.

nodes.label: Surrogate keys are constrained because they enter a regex
nodes.rationale: Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9:._-] at build time AND re-validated in VCL: a key of .* means one request dumps the entire cache onto the origin. Matching is anchored with (^|[[:space:]])key([[:space:]]|$) so a ban for t:abc does not also evict another tenant's t:abcdef.
nodes.norm_label: surrogate keys are constrained because they enter a regex

nodes.label: Literal spaces in a ban expression make invalidation never work
nodes.rationale: Varnish splits ban expressions on whitespace into <field> <operator> <argument>, so (^| )key( |$) yields the wrong token count and is rejected — yet the BAN handler still answers 200, so the purge client logs success, the queue row is marked done, and content stays stale until TTL. No test, log or metric goes red. Quoting does not help: tokenization happens before quote handling (verified on Varnish 7.5). Found only by putting Varnish in front of staging and watching X-Cache stay HIT. Guarded by a test that reads infra/varnish/default.vcl directly, because the expression is built in VCL and not in TypeScript.
nodes.norm_label: literal spaces in a ban expression make invalidation never work

nodes.label: Bun does not send non-standard HTTP methods (BAN arrives as GET)
nodes.rationale: fetch and node:http with method BAN reach Varnish as GET (verified Bun 1.3.14 against varnishlog; the same bytes over a raw socket log BAN and get 200 Banned), so every purge missed the VCL ban branch, fell through to origin, and 404'd. Wire protocol is now POST /__edge-cache-purge, with VCL still accepting real BAN for manual curl. Method was never the security control — ACL, token, and key charset validation are, at both doors. A fetchImpl mock CANNOT catch this class of bug: it inspects arguments, not the wire, so it asserts method === 'BAN' and passes forever; the transport test uses a real Bun.serve and asserts the method as RECEIVED.
nodes.norm_label: bun does not send non-standard http methods (ban arrives as get)

nodes.label: Wrong RLS GUC name killed the write path, not just the cache
nodes.rationale: sql/068 used awcms.tenant_id while withTenant() sets app.current_tenant_id (108 other policies use the correct one), so WITH CHECK evaluated NULL, INSERT was refused, and because enqueueModuleContentPurge is awaited INSIDE the content transaction without a guard, blog publish itself failed with a 500. Fixed by sql/070 and guarded by a DB-free text gate that runs in the quality job.
nodes.norm_label: wrong rls guc name killed the write path, not just the cache

nodes.label: Purge for a module with no declared surface matches nothing
nodes.rationale: Cached objects are tagged only with the key of the module that OWNS the surface — today only blog_content and theming (news_portal having been merged into blog_content by ADR-0044/#300). Enqueueing m:news_portal or m:media_library produces a ban matching no object while the queue reports sent=1. Do not add them 'just in case': the surfaces gate demands purge emission from every module that owns a surface, so the obligation appears automatically the day the surface is declared and not a second earlier.
nodes.norm_label: purge for a module with no declared surface matches nothing

nodes.label: Load pressure changes only HOW LONG, never WHETHER
nodes.rationale: pressure.ts is never an input to decideCacheability. Merging them as a 'simplification' would let a load spike turn private responses public. Related trap: the auto-activation latch is set by sample(), not record(), so a test burst without sample() in the middle never engages it.
nodes.norm_label: load pressure changes only how long, never whether

nodes.label: idn_admin_regions module (NOT ported; port spec)
nodes.rationale: Indonesian administrative-region master data sourced from cahyadsn/wilayah, registered directly in the base repo because region data is relevant to nearly every derived application, but typed base (pure reference data) rather than domain or system. Exists in awcms-mini only; issues #658-#664 were closed NOT_PLANNED as a temporary maintainer hold, so that scope must not be continued without an explicit reopen.

nodes.label: source-provenance.ts as single source of truth for source/license/caveat
nodes.rationale: One constants file holds the upstream repo URL, MIT license, and the mandatory official-reference caveat (this is a third-party community dataset, NOT an official Kemendagri export, and does not replace the operator's legal reference to the original Kepmendagri). Follow-up issues must import the constants rather than retyping the strings, so they cannot drift. Purely descriptive, so it does not violate the scaffold-only 'no import logic yet' boundary.
nodes.norm_label: source-provenance.ts as single source of truth for source/license/caveat

nodes.label: Global reference data: no tenant_id, no RLS, zero awcms_app grants
nodes.rationale: Deliberately diverges from the tenant-scoped migration template; both tables were added to RLS_FREE_TABLES and ALLOWED_GLOBAL_TABLE_GRANTS or the readiness checks fail once the tables exist. migration 013's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES auto-grants awcms_app on CREATE TABLE, so the schema migration REVOKEs it in the same transaction — schema-only issues have no code path reading these tables, and later issues add exactly the grants their new code path needs.
nodes.norm_label: global reference data: no tenant_id, no rls, zero awcms_app grants

nodes.label: Single active dataset via partial unique index on status
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE INDEX ... (status) WHERE status = 'active': every indexed row holds the same value, so uniqueness on that column caps active datasets at one — the standard Postgres singleton-flag idiom, needing no separate boolean or computed column, and the same index is the fastest path for the default 'find the active dataset' query. Verified against a real database including that superseding a row reopens the slot.
nodes.norm_label: single active dataset via partial unique index on status

nodes.label: .gitattributes binary override preserves vendored bytes and checksums
nodes.rationale: Upstream db/wilayah.sql uses CRLF while the repo convention (* text=auto eol=lf) would normalize it on git add, silently changing vendor bytes and invalidating the checksums recorded in the same commit. Marking the whole upstream/ subtree binary disables EOL normalization; verified by comparing git show hashes to the freshly cloned files. New vendored files under that subtree inherit the rule automatically.
nodes.norm_label: .gitattributes binary override preserves vendored bytes and checksums

nodes.label: integration_hub module (NOT ported; port spec)
nodes.rationale: Generic provider-neutral integration boundary in awcms-mini: signed inbound webhooks, normalized events via domain_event_runtime, outbound subscriptions with retry/dead-letter, and provider health. It calls no business-provider API — only generic fetch() to a tenant-configured target_url and passive webhook receipt — and never calls a provider inside a database transaction. Inbound tenant resolution goes through a narrow SECURITY DEFINER bootstrap function before any withTenant transaction, because the inbound endpoint is public.

nodes.label: Two-layer SSRF guard with redirect: manual re-validation
nodes.rationale: Write-time validation blocks private/link-local/metadata/reserved literals and known metadata hostnames; dispatch-time re-validates AND checks every DNS-resolved address, and critically calls fetch with redirect: 'manual', re-validating every Location header through the same check before following (bounded by MAX_REDIRECT_HOPS). The earlier version trusted fetch's default redirect-follow and only validated the original target_url, so a subscription could 302 to 169.254.169.254 — a 100%-reliable bypass with no timing race (fixed before merge, PR #784). Response bodies are byte-capped inside the same timeout window. Residual documented gap: resolved IPs are not pinned for the actual call, so DNS-rebinding TOCTOU remains open — narrow and timing-dependent, distinct from the closed redirect bug.
nodes.norm_label: two-layer ssrf guard with redirect: manual re-validation

nodes.label: Replay protection as a real DB constraint
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (tenant_id, endpoint_id, replay_key) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: zero rows affected means already processed, a new row means genuinely new and the normalized payload plus appendDomainEvent happen in the SAME transaction. Not an in-memory check, so it survives restarts and multi-instance deployments.
nodes.norm_label: replay protection as a real db constraint

nodes.label: INTEGRATION_HUB_ prefix validation on secretReference
nodes.rationale: Closes a confused-deputy equality oracle: unrestricted env:<ANY_VAR> let a tenant with only ordinary endpoint/subscription permissions point at an unrelated process-wide secret and use repeated signed-webhook attempts (200 vs 401) as a boolean equality oracle against it. Secrets are only ever pointers; the resolved value is used in memory for exactly one HMAC computation and never returned or logged.

nodes.label: timingSafeEqualHex for signature verification
nodes.rationale: Uses node:crypto timingSafeEqual, never === on signatures (=== is a timing side channel); same pattern as sync-storage's sync-hmac. Key rotation keeps an overlap window so requests signed with the previous secret still verify until it expires.

nodes.label: Stale 'sending' lease reclaim
nodes.rationale: The claim query also reclaims deliveries stuck in sending whose 2-minute lease expired, so a worker crash mid-fetch no longer strands a delivery forever (reviewer finding, PR #784). Dead-lettered deliveries are replayed by creating a NEW row referencing the old one, never by mutating or re-queueing the old row.

nodes.label: integrationHubOutboundFanoutConsumer
nodes.rationale: Registered in domain-event-runtime's consumer-registry array — the same additive extension point other modules use to become producers; this is the first real third-party consumer. Runs in the SAME transaction as the source event commit as a DB-only handler with zero network calls, creating pending delivery rows; the actual HTTP dispatch is a separate worker step outside any transaction (ADR-0006).

nodes.label: Jualanku.info porting plan (ADR-0045)
nodes.rationale: P0 with ZERO code: no jualanku modules, tables, migrations, routes or permissions; listModules() still returns 20. The skill exists to hold decisions that cannot be inferred from code and are expensive to guess wrong. Heavy reuse is mandated (blog_content, seo_distribution, site_search, media_library, theming, tenant_domain, visitor_analytics, comments, data_lifecycle, email, workflow_approval with sodRules for maker-checker payout, form_drafts). One bounded context per PR, each carrying migration, permission seed, OpenAPI fragment, negative tests, docs and changeset.

nodes.label: Merchant is a business scope, not a new ABAC attribute
nodes.rationale: ABAC_ATTRIBUTES is a CLOSED allow-list — unknown attributes are invalid at authoring time and deny at evaluation. subject.merchantIds/resource.merchantId are absent and must not be added: widening it for one product destroys the property that makes it valuable. Instead reuse the existing resource.businessScopeId plus the ADR-0030 scope-hierarchy port whose base returns resolved:false fail-closed.
nodes.norm_label: merchant is a business scope, not a new abac attribute

nodes.label: RLS separates tenants, not merchants
nodes.rationale: One organizer tenant holds many merchants, so merchant isolation needs THREE layers: tenant RLS, effective-dated scope grants, and an ownership predicate in every query. Never infer isolation from FORCE RLS alone, and always test as the awcms_app role — on a superuser PaaS, RLS can be inert while migrations stay green.

nodes.label: The browser never calls awcms directly (awcms-astro BFF)
nodes.rationale: The BFF may orchestrate and project but decides no ownership, entitlement, or status transition. If a check exists only in the BFF, that check does not exist.
nodes.norm_label: the browser never calls awcms directly (awcms-astro bff)

nodes.label: Five bounded contexts, not seven
nodes.rationale: jualanku_directory, _catalog_growth, _affiliate, _commercial, _trust_operations. Boundaries follow invariants and data ownership, not menu structure.

nodes.label: The real session gap is cross-origin introspection, not cookie support
nodes.rationale: resolveAuthInputs() already accepts a header OR an httpOnly cookie — that is how admin SSR works today. What is missing is a session introspection contract for a DIFFERENT origin, since /api/v1/auth/me is deliberately bearer-only.
nodes.norm_label: the real session gap is cross-origin introspection, not cookie support

nodes.label: Permissions may only use existing AccessAction values
nodes.rationale: There is no submit/verify/payout. An action outside the union yields a permission that is never seeded and a silent deny against the tenant owner, green in CI because nothing tests it. Related traps: a descriptor's permissions array grants nothing to EXISTING tenants (each module needs its own seed migration plus a role-permission backfill), cross-table tenant-scoped FKs must be composite (tenant_id, id) because plain FKs bypass RLS, and check:docs fails on sql/NNN references to migrations that do not exist yet.
nodes.norm_label: permissions may only use existing accessaction values

nodes.label: media_library module (ADR-0036 ownership inversion)
nodes.rationale: Exists in this repo (migrations sql/052-sql/054). A System Foundation (type: system, isCore: false, deps tenant_admin + identity_access) owning the per-tenant media registry, presigned R2 upload/finalize/cancel, verification, orphan lifecycle, the news-media:reconcile job, and enforcement activation. Born by moving the registry OUT of news_portal, not by additive porting; that origin module was later merged into blog_content, so blog_content is now the ad-placement consumer. Not yet ported: micro steps 5b/5c/5d (/admin/media browser, srcset, PDF).

nodes.label: MediaLibraryPort (_shared/ports/media-library-port.ts)
nodes.rationale: Three methods (isManagedMediaEnforcementActiveForTenant, isMediaReferenceSafe, resolveMediaReferences) with a real adapter that imports ONLY from media_library — never from blog-content, which would be the ADR-0013 §1 inversion that was deleted. Any port/capability change must update _shared/capability-contract-versions.ts and the family compatibility manifest key-for-key or family:conformance:check goes red.

nodes.label: One-way managed-media enforcement (no disable path)
nodes.rationale: The per-tenant flag has exactly one writer, reachable only from a sanctioned entry point that runs the readiness gate first and audits. POST can only turn enforcement ON. Adding an enforcement.disable action, any unmark/clear function, or a DELETE against the tenant-state table is forbidden because it restores the exploit recorded in sql/043's header (a tenant switching off its own media validation); a dedicated test enforces this. Enforcement is active only when deployment readiness AND the per-tenant flag agree; failed readiness is fail-closed without a DB query.

nodes.label: Presigned direct-to-R2 upload / finalize / cancel
nodes.rationale: Finalize performs a real R2 GET plus magic-byte MIME sniffing and SHA-256, is high-risk and Idempotency-Key gated, and is guarded by media_library.media.* permissions. Object key prefix news-media/{tenantId}/... is preserved.

nodes.label: awcms_news_media_objects name preserved (hard composite FK)
nodes.rationale: The table was NOT renamed when ownership inverted, because awcms_news_portal_ad_placements holds a hard composite FK to it; internal symbols (fetchNewsMediaObjectById, NewsMediaObjectView, ...) were likewise kept. With news_portal merged away, the awcms_news_* naming is no longer a hint about any module.

nodes.label: NEWS_MEDIA_R2_* kept separate from sync-storage's R2_*
nodes.rationale: Env var names, table names and the news-media:reconcile command are all deliberately retained by ADR-0036 §3/§4; the media R2 config must stay distinct from sync-storage's R2_*.
nodes.norm_label: news_media_r2_* kept separate from sync-storage's r2_*

nodes.label: Module Management system
nodes.rationale: Owns the base registry, registry composition validation, per-tenant enable/disable lifecycle, settings, permission sync/status, navigation, job registry and health. module_management is the only isCore:true module — it cannot be disabled, which is the primary admin-lockout preventer.

nodes.label: Sync-first FK rule
nodes.rationale: awcms_tenant_modules, _module_settings and _module_health_checks all FK to awcms_modules.module_key, and registering a module in src/modules/index.ts does NOT create the registry row. Every tenant-scoped mutation needing that row calls syncModuleDescriptors(tx) itself — never assume an operator ran POST /api/v1/modules/sync first. Consequence: health signal db_registry_synced can legitimately fail on a freshly migrated instance while POST .../health/check shows pass for the same signal at the same moment, because it syncs as a side effect of writing history.

nodes.label: Dependency graph for enable/disable
nodes.rationale: The graph is ALWAYS read from listModules() in code, never from awcms_module_dependencies (a cache of the last sync that can be stale). Error codes: MODULE_NOT_FOUND, MODULE_ALREADY_ENABLED/_DISABLED, MODULE_DEPENDENCY_MISSING, MODULE_DEPENDENCY_DISABLED, MODULE_REVERSE_DEPENDENCY_ACTIVE, MODULE_DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, MODULE_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE, CORE_MODULE_CANNOT_BE_DISABLED.

nodes.label: validateModuleDependencyGraph: registry-wide DAG validator
nodes.rationale: hasDependencyCycle only ever ran for the single module being enabled, so a real 3-node cycle among tenant_admin/profile_identity/identity_access survived as long as the registry was never iterated whole. The new validator detects self_dependency, duplicate_dependency, missing_dependency and cycles (full Kahn, not one-point DFS) and reports all four rather than stopping at the first; it gates modules:dag:check and modules:sync (which refuses to touch a row when the graph is broken). The real fix was emptying tenant_admin.dependencies: its setup-wizard write into other modules' tables was a CALL-TIME need expressed as a static dependency — that orchestration is now an explicit composition-root function, and new cross-module orchestration must do the same rather than adding a dependencies edge.

nodes.label: capabilities (source-level) vs dependencies (lifecycle)
nodes.rationale: capabilities.provides/consumes documents ports-and-adapters IMPORT relationships only; dependencies remains the sole field read by the cycle/enable/disable logic. A consuming module never imports another module's application/domain tree — only the port interface, with a concrete adapter injected by the caller (the route handler as composition root). optional:true means the consumer degrades safely when the capability resolves to 'not applicable' for a tenant, not that the code compiles without the other module (this is a monolith).

nodes.label: Two composition-root variants; pick by security stakes
nodes.rationale: Variant 1 always injects the concrete adapter with no tenant enable/disable check, relying on a port designed fail-closed/no-op-safe. Variant 2 explicitly calls resolveModuleEnabled first and falls back to the consumer's default adapter when the providing module is disabled for that tenant. Choose variant 2 when the consumed capability decides an authorization/security outcome — degrading 'safely' through the port alone risks silently consulting data owned by a module the tenant already disabled.
nodes.norm_label: two composition-root variants; pick by security stakes

nodes.label: Settings shallow merge plus secret-shaped value rejection
nodes.rationale: PATCH merges shallowly into the existing tenantOverride (unmentioned keys unchanged) because here the whole request body IS the settings resource, unlike featureFlags which replaces a named field of another resource. Secret-like KEYS are rejected at request time (400 SETTINGS_SENSITIVE_KEY_REJECTED) rather than stored and redacted on read, and credential-shaped VALUES are rejected too (JWT, PEM block, AWS key id, raw Bearer/Basic header, user:pass@ connection string) — deliberately conservative so ordinary labels/URLs/flags are never wrongly refused; the error names only the key path, never the value.
nodes.norm_label: settings shallow merge plus secret-shaped value rejection

nodes.label: Route ownership lives in api.routes, not basePath
nodes.rationale: basePath is a display prefix; api.routes is a list because ownership genuinely is not one prefix (/api/v1/tenant is split between tenant_domain and module_management, and non-API public surfaces count too). NEVER write basePath /api/v1: tenant_admin once did and swallowed 36 routes belonging to other modules. A coverage gate alone is insufficient — a prefix matching everything leaves zero unclaimed routes, so the gate goes green while the answer is wrong; /, /api and /api/v1 are rejected explicitly. modules:routes:check demands every src/pages file except /admin/** map to exactly one module or appear in PLATFORM_ROUTES with a reason; /admin/** is deliberately excluded because the navigation registry test already binds it and claiming it twice would create two sources of truth for one fact.
nodes.norm_label: route ownership lives in api.routes, not basepath

nodes.label: navigation is one source; the sidebar renders from the registry
nodes.rationale: Consumed four ways: descriptor-sync writes it to awcms_module_navigation, the navigation registry serves it via GET /api/v1/modules, composition validates path conflicts, and AdminLayout renders the sidebar from it. The previous version of this guidance was WRONG after the rewire — it told authors to also add links to a static navSections array that no longer exists. Section placement comes from DEFAULT_MODULE_TYPE, which BEATS the entry's group; new modules must appear in that map or the gate refuses. The bidirectional gate requires every navigation path to have a real page and every /admin page to be claimed by exactly one descriptor, proven red for all three violation classes — so declare navigation and create the page in the same PR.
nodes.norm_label: navigation is one source; the sidebar renders from the registry

nodes.label: Permission sync status: never auto-fix orphaned
nodes.rationale: The report is read-only (synced/missing/orphaned/mismatched_description). Now that all 20 modules declare permissions, orphaned is no longer background noise — it is a real signal. The twelve permanently-orphaned email rows before #251 were a persistent false positive, and persistent false positives train readers to ignore a drift report, the one thing a drift report must not do. Fix by aligning the descriptor or adding a seed migration, never by DELETE without an explicit admin decision.
nodes.norm_label: permission sync status: never auto-fix orphaned

nodes.label: Tenant module presets
nodes.rationale: applyModulePreset sets a tenant's module states to a profile by 100% reusing evaluate/enable/disable — it never writes awcms_tenant_modules directly. It both enables and disables: modules absent from the preset and not 'protected' (isCore plus its transitive dependency closure, computed dynamically) are disabled leaves-first, skipped rather than forced when still required by something enabled. Idempotent.

nodes.label: MODULE_CONTRACT_VERSION 2.3.0 and descriptor-list seams
nodes.rationale: ADR-0034 took it to 2.0.0 (breaking: derived-registry types deleted); since then three additive MINORs, all descriptor-LIST seams discovered by aggregators through listModules() rather than capability provides — because multiple providers are expected there and a second provider would trip capability_provider_conflict: 2.1.0 dataLifecycle, 2.2.0 searchSources (ADR-0040), 2.3.0 commentableResources (ADR-0041). Every bump must also update the family compatibility manifest pin or family:conformance:check goes red.

nodes.label: Health: passive GET, explicit POST
nodes.rationale: GET returns only cheap generic signals and NEVER calls an external provider, so it is safe to poll; POST adds a timeout-bounded live provider check where a module has one and writes history. New provider checks go only in POST, bounded and non-throwing, with detail always a fixed generic string rather than a raw error message.

nodes.label: ADR-0034: derived pathway removed, base registry composition remains
nodes.rationale: awcms is a template used directly: no derived repo, application-registry.ts, extension:check, extension.manifest.json, or 900-999 migration namespace. Domain/website modules live directly in src/modules/. Surviving enforcement over the BASE registry: duplicate_module_key, capability_provider_conflict/_missing, deployment_profile_incompatible, navigation_path_conflict, invalid_job_descriptor and the DAG checks. Deleted (derived-only): prohibited_base_override, invalid_module_type, migration_namespace_overlap, mergeModuleRegistries. Also: doc 21's '23 modules' must not be read as registry contents — listModules() returns 20, and five platform-evolution modules with Accepted ADRs have no code.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0034: derived pathway removed, base registry composition remains

nodes.label: New module scaffold structure
nodes.rationale: src/modules/<kebab>/ with module.ts, domain/, application/, infrastructure/ and a full README (other modules run 94-854 lines, not a short summary). key is snake_case, folder kebab-case, type PascalCase. Register in src/modules/index.ts, then modules:compose:check and modules:composition:inventory:check must be green; there is no extension:check any more.

nodes.label: ModuleDescriptor template (defineModule)
nodes.rationale: openApiPath points at the module's own fragment (ADR-0026), not the generated bundle; AsyncAPI is still one shared file. Optional fields (isCore, permissions, navigation, settings, jobs, health, compatibility, maintainers) may only be declared AFTER the corresponding feature actually exists — never claim an unimplemented capability, following module_management's own one-at-a-time precedent.

nodes.label: API routes live in src/pages, never inside the module folder
nodes.rationale: No module has an api/ folder; real routes sit at src/pages/api/v1/<resource>/ (Astro file-based routing) and import services/repositories from the module's application/infrastructure layers.
nodes.norm_label: api routes live in src/pages, never inside the module folder

nodes.label: The 20 registered modules (and what is NOT registered)
nodes.rationale: Registered in index.ts order: logging, tenant-admin, profile-identity, identity-access, module-management, domain-event-runtime, sync-storage, workflow-approval, email, reporting, theming, media-library, blog-content, tenant-domain, visitor-analytics, data-lifecycle, seo-distribution, form-drafts, site-search, comments. Absent despite Accepted ADRs or existing skills: data-exchange, document-infrastructure, integration-hub, organization-structure, reference-data, social-publishing, idn-admin-regions, and news-portal (merged into blog_content). Verify with listModules() rather than quoting any document.
nodes.norm_label: the 20 registered modules (and what is not registered)

nodes.label: Module admission governance check (doc 21)
nodes.rationale: Before scaffolding anything new, read the admission governance doc (Core / System / Official Optional / Derived Application / External Integration categories, decision tree, dependency and security-review criteria) and fill the module proposal template on the GitHub issue. Single-business-domain modules still have to pass the decision tree.

nodes.label: news_portal module (historic; merged into blog_content)
nodes.rationale: src/modules/news-portal/ is deleted, index.ts no longer loads it, and /api/v1/news-portal does not exist. Its features live on inside blog_content (homepage-section composer, verified media_object_id ad placements) and its table names are preserved. The skill body is retained as a PRE-MERGE SPECIFICATION because §640 is still cited by blog_content's README for content-quality rules — every file path inside it is history, not a location in today's code.

nodes.label: Key decision #1: media R2 bucket separate from sync-storage
nodes.rationale: sync-storage's R2 is a PRIVATE machine-to-machine object queue; news media is public, browser-fetched, custom-domain and CORS-enabled — fundamentally different. Separate buckets stop a public misconfiguration in one function from exposing the other's private objects, and separate credentials bound the blast radius in both directions. The same Cloudflare account is fine; the bucket and API token must differ. Enforced (not merely documented) by a separation check wired into config:validate and a critical security:readiness check, which is why the env prefix NEWS_MEDIA_R2_* was chosen over the issue body's suggested R2_* names.
nodes.norm_label: key decision #1: media r2 bucket separate from sync-storage

nodes.label: Key decision #2: no local fallback, no temp file
nodes.rationale: Image bytes are never written to local disk, neither as a failure fallback nor as an intermediate during upload — the inverse of sync-storage, which is correct for its offline-first case. Because the mode structurally has no local-upload path to disable, the acceptance criterion was met with a STRUCTURAL test that greps the module tree for Bun.write/fs.writeFile/LOCAL_STORAGE_PATH and fails loudly the moment any PR adds one, rather than with a runtime flag.
nodes.norm_label: key decision #2: no local fallback, no temp file

nodes.label: Key decision #3: object keys never carry PII or the original filename
nodes.rationale: Format news-media/{tenantId}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{uuid}.{ext} with uuid from crypto.randomUUID() and ext derived from the VALIDATED mime via an explicit 4-type map (never mime.split('/')[1], which would guess); an unmapped mime throws loudly. original_filename is a separate display-only column. Validated in three layers: application at generation, a Postgres CHECK referencing the row's own tenant_id (defence against direct INSERTs bypassing the helper), and a structural unit test. Public URLs are built only from the trusted configured base URL plus the server-generated key, never from client input.
nodes.norm_label: key decision #3: object keys never carry pii or the original filename

nodes.label: Key decision #4: pending/confirmed status does not control storage access
nodes.rationale: Once an object is PUT to R2 it is publicly reachable through the custom domain; the Postgres status does not block storage-level reads. Mitigations are the unguessable key, editorial content only ever pointing at confirmed objects, and a lifecycle job sweeping stale pending objects. Never implement a control that assumes the Postgres status already prevents public access.
nodes.norm_label: key decision #4: pending/confirmed status does not control storage access

nodes.label: Key decision #5: image/svg+xml forbidden by default
nodes.rationale: Default MIME allow-list is jpeg/png/webp/gif; SVG is excluded because of embedded-script XSS. Allowing it requires a dedicated sanitization pipeline and a separate decision, not an allow-list edit in some issue.
nodes.norm_label: key decision #5: image/svg+xml forbidden by default

nodes.label: Finalize does a full GET plus magic-byte sniff and server-side checksum
nodes.rationale: The issue body's 'verify via HEAD/metadata' was deliberately NOT followed as stale against the post-review architecture. Real order: headObject (cheap existence plus real Content-Length, short-circuiting before GET), full getObject, magic-byte sniff over an allow-list, SHA-256 over THOSE SAME BYTES, then the finalize decision. The MIME verdict always comes from sniffing; a client-claimed checksum (optional, in the FINALIZE body rather than create, since the schema has only one checksum column holding the server-computed value) is only ever a transport-corruption check and never replaces sniffing. Proven by an integration test uploading real HTML/<script> bytes behind a .jpg key and asserting 422 UPLOAD_VERIFICATION_FAILED with reason mime_not_recognized plus an audit event. The verification logic was extracted out of the Astro route precisely to expose a deps.createR2Client seam, since a route's fixed (context) => Response signature has no injection point.
nodes.norm_label: finalize does a full get plus magic-byte sniff and server-side checksum

nodes.label: TOCTOU size-cap fix (readCappedStream)
nodes.rationale: Critical finding: arrayBuffer() buffered the whole object into memory BEFORE its size was checked, and because a presigned PUT URL is reusable an attacker could overwrite the object with a huge file between headObject (reporting a small size) and getObject, causing OOM. The read now cancels the stream exactly when the cap is exceeded and never accumulates more than maxBytes, and the streamed sizeExceeded verdict is AUTHORITATIVE over a possibly-stale head size.

nodes.label: Atomic uploaded-claim as mutual exclusion
nodes.rationale: High finding: N concurrent finalize calls with DIFFERENT Idempotency-Keys on the SAME object each paid their own HEAD+GET. Fix: the pending_upload -> uploaded transition is an atomic claim inside the precheck transaction BEFORE any R2 call — its WHERE status = 'pending_upload' is the mutual-exclusion primitive, since Postgres serializes concurrent UPDATEs of one row. The winner proceeds; losers get a cheap 409 without ever touching R2. Consequence to preserve: the claim is now held across a SEPARATE DB transaction while the R2 call runs, which requires an explicit revert path back to pending_upload.

nodes.label: §681: capability ports replacing direct cross-module imports
nodes.rationale: Fixed a real SOURCE-LEVEL cycle (not just a dependencies-array one) by introducing minimal ports-and-adapters with the route handler as composition root, so neither module imports the other's application/domain tree. Historic in the sense that the two modules are now one; the live equivalent port is MediaLibraryPort from media_library.
nodes.norm_label: §681: capability ports replacing direct cross-module imports

nodes.label: owner_resource_type/owner_resource_id: polymorphic reference without FK
nodes.rationale: A deliberately loose (text, uuid) pair following the existing audit-event and workflow-instance idiom (stricter here: uuid plus a CHECK enum), so one registry serves every consumer without a per-consumer FK and without the migration depending on blog_content's schema. Both columns stay NULL until status='attached', enforced by CHECK and by only accepting the transition from verified. Latent security finding to close before any real attach endpoint ships: because there is no FK, the attach function will happily bind to ANY uuid, including another tenant's or one that never existed, so an ownership+tenant verification query must run inside the same tenant-scoped transaction, with an explicit cross-tenant rejection test.

nodes.label: §640: content quality checklist with R2 image requirements
nodes.rationale: Follows the #636 single-gate pattern rather than blanket-tightening all of blog_content, reuses ONE mediaPort.resolveMediaReferences call instead of re-deriving R2 verification, and keeps five security rules that tenant policy can never downgrade in any environment — stricter than the issue's literal request. Tenant policy is stored in the existing blog settings jsonb rather than through a new mechanism, and the scheduled-publish worker was restructured from a bulk UPDATE into a per-post loop to evaluate it.
nodes.norm_label: §640: content quality checklist with r2 image requirements

nodes.label: §641: automatic internal tag linking via HTMLRewriter
nodes.rationale: HTML tree parsing with Bun HTMLRewriter rather than regex over raw strings; matching happens in the ESCAPED domain and text is never decoded; word boundaries are Unicode-aware rather than \b; two levels of cap (per-tag and per-post). Tenant policy lives in a DEDICATED table, unlike #640's settings-jsonb choice. Field note: Bun.SQL does not auto-deserialize Postgres array columns — a real trap found during integration testing.
nodes.norm_label: §641: automatic internal tag linking via htmlrewriter

nodes.label: Readiness gate must not be bypassed by calling the generic preset engine
nodes.rationale: The sanctioned wrapper runs an env readiness evaluation and audits both rejection and success; the generic applyModulePreset knows nothing about R2, so calling it directly with the preset name would activate it with NO gate and NO audit. Inert while no caller exists, but the first caller must add a STRUCTURAL grep test proving the preset literal only ever flows through the wrapper — code-review discipline is not enough. The wrapper also performs no ABAC check by design (the caller's responsibility), and its readiness is deployment-global env state, not per-tenant module state, so it can report ready for a tenant that has since disabled the modules it needs.
