nodes.rationale: Moderation holds publication without deleting data; appeals are decided by someone other than the original decider; a consumer complaint channel must exist before go-live (UU 8/1999); onboarding assignments are the time-boxed scope grant source for accompaniment agents.
nodes.norm_label: jualanku_trust_operations context (verification, moderation, complaints, appeals, onboarding assignments)

nodes.label: Draft ModuleDescriptor for a Jualanku module (MODULE_CONTRACT_VERSION 2.4.0)
nodes.rationale: routes declare route ownership (modules:routes:check) and only the owning module may write its tables (modules:table-writes:check); capabilities.provides changes the capability graph, not the dependency DAG, so the DAG stays acyclic; every new domain module needs an admission ADR.
nodes.norm_label: draft moduledescriptor for a jualanku module (module_contract_version 2.4.0)

nodes.label: Table conventions: awcms_jualanku_<context>_<entity>, FORCE RLS, numeric money
nodes.rationale: The long prefix is chosen so module ownership is readable from the table name; merchant_id is named identically in every context so the ownership predicate can be reviewed with one grep; migration numbers are deliberately NOT written into the doc because check:docs fails on references to files that do not exist and applied migrations are immutable.
nodes.norm_label: table conventions: awcms_jualanku_<context>_<entity>, force rls, numeric money

nodes.label: Composite FK (tenant_id, id) because plain FKs bypass RLS
nodes.rationale: A normal FK evaluates outside row-level security and becomes a cross-tenant leak path; FK targets therefore need UNIQUE (tenant_id, id).
nodes.norm_label: composite fk (tenant_id, id) because plain fks bypass rls

nodes.label: One table = one writing module; cross-context only via service/port/read model/event
nodes.rationale: commercial and affiliate must not depend on catalog_growth; they connect through events (conversion.recorded, subscription.activated) and read models. No context writes another context's tables, not even from a job.
nodes.norm_label: one table = one writing module; cross-context only via service/port/read model/event

nodes.label: Personal-data classes and retention treatment
nodes.rationale: Bank/NIK/NPWP/phone/email stored normalized+hashed and shown masked per purpose; verification evidence via media_library with audited access and never a public URL; clicks/analytics privacy-minimized with short retention; ledger/invoice/payout kept long for bookkeeping obligations and subject to legal hold.

nodes.label: Three API namespaces, one rule implementation
nodes.rationale: /api/v1/jualanku/public/**, /portal/**, /admin/** all call the SAME application service; only authentication, authorization, accepted input surface, and response projection differ. A business rule written twice is a defect regardless of whether the copies currently agree.
nodes.norm_label: three api namespaces, one rule implementation

nodes.label: Target endpoint inventory (public / portal merchant / portal affiliate / admin)
nodes.rationale: Public merchant detail returns 404 (not 403) for draft/held rows; directory search reuses site_search rather than a new search endpoint; displayed affiliate balance is available ledger balance after holding period/reversal/dispute, not total conversions; /admin/payouts is SoD-gated maker != approver.
nodes.norm_label: target endpoint inventory (public / portal merchant / portal affiliate / admin)

nodes.label: Binding minimum API contract (envelope, error codes, pagination, idempotency, concurrency)
nodes.rationale: Keyset cursors must carry created_at as full-precision TEXT because Postgres microsecond vs JS millisecond precision silently skips rows; idempotency is mandatory for payout/invoice/publish/import/interaction ingest; ETag/version optimistic locking for profile, catalog and moderation cases; security headers come from middleware, not astro.config.
nodes.norm_label: binding minimum api contract (envelope, error codes, pagination, idempotency, concurrency)

nodes.label: Jualanku domain events as the only automatic cross-context path
nodes.rationale: merchant.published, merchant.verification_decided, offering.published, interaction.recorded, conversion.recorded/reversed, payout.decided, subscription.changed — each with declared producer and typical consumers, and each declared in AsyncAPI with PII classification, retry and dead-letter.
nodes.norm_label: jualanku domain events as the only automatic cross-context path

nodes.label: Deliberately not built in the early phase
nodes.rationale: No marketplace checkout/escrow/wallet/logistics/multi-merchant transactions, no own search endpoint, no second identity system in the portal, no public endpoint that accepts merchantId as an ownership determinant, and no outbound webhooks before contract/retry policy/data classification are approved.
nodes.norm_label: deliberately not built in the early phase

nodes.label: What awcms session support already is (often misread)
nodes.rationale: Login already returns a token AND sets httpOnly awcms_session + awcms_tenant_id cookies; resolveAuthInputs() accepts bearer+tenant header OR cookie (header wins), which is how admin SSR authenticates today; only GET /api/v1/auth/me is bearer-only. Sessions are stored as token hashes, revocable, and MFA step-up rotates them.
nodes.norm_label: what awcms session support already is (often misread)

nodes.label: Cross-origin session contract (the real gap)
nodes.rationale: The missing piece is not 'cookie support' but a session contract for a DIFFERENT origin: the awcms_session cookie belongs to the awcms origin and a browser on jualanku.info will never send it, and must not. The browser holds only a jualanku_portal httpOnly cookie; the BFF maps it server-side to an awcms token.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/auth/session — safe-claims introspection endpoint (to be added, owned by identity_access)
nodes.rationale: Called by the BFF, never the browser. Returns only identityId/tenantId/displayName/roles/assuranceLevel/expiresAt/scopes; never a token, token hash, password state, MFA secret, recovery code, or raw email/phone. Invalid, expired and revoked sessions all produce the identical 401 AUTH_REQUIRED so it cannot be used as an oracle. The rejected alternative was letting public browsers call /api/v1/** directly with cross-site cookies, which moves tenant selection, CSRF and CORS to the client.
nodes.norm_label: get /api/v1/auth/session — safe-claims introspection endpoint (to be added, owned by identity_access)

nodes.label: BFF obligations (cookie, token storage, CSRF, tenant, logout order, rotation, revocation)
nodes.rationale: CSRF needs Origin/Referer check PLUS a double-submit/synchronizer token, not either alone. Logout must call awcms logout FIRST and only then clear the portal cookie — the reverse order leaves the session alive. The BFF keeps no session list of its own; awcms stays the revocation source of truth.
nodes.norm_label: bff obligations (cookie, token storage, csrf, tenant, logout order, rotation, revocation)

nodes.label: Portal session threat model
nodes.rationale: XSS token theft closed by never putting tokens in JS; confused-deputy closed by an explicit upstream route list with no generic passthrough; tenant tampering closed by server-derived tenant; private-to-cache/sitemap leakage closed by no-store plus the cache surface gate; account/merchant enumeration closed by uniform responses and 404 anti-oracle.

nodes.label: Seven tests that must accompany the session contract
nodes.rationale: Field-by-field introspection assertions so a newly leaked field turns the test red; identical response shape for revoked vs expired; client tenant header ignored; portal logout really kills the awcms session; step-up rotates the token and the old one dies.
nodes.norm_label: seven tests that must accompany the session contract

nodes.label: Definition of porting (translate intent, never copy WordPress markup)
nodes.rationale: Porting translates user goals, information hierarchy, visual patterns, copy, states and component behaviour from the Elementor prototype into Astro components and screen specs. Not one line of WordPress DOM/CSS class/widget/shortcode/plugin/data model is carried over; placeholders and sensitive demo data are REMOVEd rather than migrated.
nodes.norm_label: definition of porting (translate intent, never copy wordpress markup)

nodes.label: Migration disposition codes (PORT / REDESIGN / DYNAMIC / REMOVE / DEFER)
nodes.rationale: A per-route/section worksheet is produced before the first screen, each row carrying route, section, disposition, data owner and accessibility notes.
nodes.norm_label: migration disposition codes (port / redesign / dynamic / remove / defer)

nodes.label: Reuse AWCMS design tokens via theming, no new token system
nodes.rationale: Solid fills with white text must use the -strong variants because plain tokens fail AA contrast in some combinations; verification/payout/moderation status is never colour-only; new tokens require written justification and a fresh contrast audit.
nodes.norm_label: reuse awcms design tokens via theming, no new token system

nodes.label: Jualanku internal admin screens under /admin/jualanku/**
nodes.rationale: Registered through the module descriptor's navigation array because the admin menu is built from the registry and a menu entry pointing at a 404 turns the navigation test red. Merchants and affiliates have no route, navigation entry, role, or session audience into any of these screens. CSP rule: no inline script — scripts are imported and bundled.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.2 AA baseline (ISO/IEC 40500:2025)
nodes.rationale: Raised from the 2.1 AA of the previous template. Keyboard operability with visible focus, 44 CSS px touch targets, server-side validation (client validation is not a control), status never colour-only, prefers-reduced-motion turns decorative animation OFF rather than speeding it up, mobile-first from 360 px.

nodes.label: P0–P6 phase roadmap with exit criteria
nodes.rationale: Each phase decomposes into atomic units of work — one bounded context (or one surface slice) per PR carrying migration + seed + OpenAPI fragment + tests + docs + changeset. P6 scale only after retention, quality, security and unit economics stabilise.
nodes.norm_label: p0–p6 phase roadmap with exit criteria

nodes.label: Blocking quality gates (existing repo gates + Jualanku-specific ones)
nodes.rationale: Full bun run check plus security:readiness and family:conformance:check; RLS isolation verified as awcms_app, not superuser. Jualanku adds: 100% endpoints in OpenAPI with a security scheme, 100% tenant tables FORCE RLS with isolation tests, 100% portal mutations through BFF+CSRF+authz+validation+audit+correlation ID, zero bearer tokens in browser storage, zero private routes in sitemap/public cache, zero placeholders/demo PII, OWASP ASVS 5.0 L2 minimum for portal and admin.
nodes.norm_label: blocking quality gates (existing repo gates + jualanku-specific ones)

nodes.label: Jualanku KPI framework and North Star
nodes.rationale: North Star is monthly active merchants with a published page AND at least one meaningful interaction — deliberately conjunctive so a published-but-dead page does not count.
nodes.norm_label: jualanku kpi framework and north star

nodes.label: GO / PIVOT / PAUSE / STOP criteria
nodes.rationale: PAUSE triggers are all security/correctness invariants: browser-manipulable session/tenant context, unproven cross-merchant authorization, private responses still cacheable/indexable, commission without ledger/hold/refund/tax/maker-checker. STOP covers marketplace checkout/escrow/wallet before PMF and any feature without owner, contract, lifecycle, permission, audit, KPI and exit criteria.

nodes.label: Standards baseline (ISO/IEC 27001/27002/27005/27701/27018/15408, OWASP ASVS 5.0, WCAG 2.2)
nodes.rationale: ISO/IEC 15408 is used only as a concept (Target of Evaluation, Security Target, assurance evidence) for session/authorization components — it is not a UI checklist and not a substitute for 27001/ASVS. No EAL claim, no 'Common Criteria certified' claim, and no ISO certification claim in product or marketing material. ISO/IEC 27017 is on transition watch.

nodes.label: Indonesian regulatory mapping (UU 27/2022 PDP, UU 1/2024 ITE, PP 71/2019, PP 80/2019 PMSE, Permendag 19/2026, UU 8/1999)
nodes.rationale: PMSE classification must never be assumed from branding — Finance/Risk/Compliance writes a legal memo based on the ACTUAL shipped features (transaction flow, ads, affiliate, payments, and the platform's role toward merchants/consumers).
nodes.norm_label: indonesian regulatory mapping (uu 27/2022 pdp, uu 1/2024 ite, pp 71/2019, pp 80/2019 pmse, permendag 19/2026, uu 8/1999)

nodes.label: Correction 1 — news_portal was MERGED, not 'not yet built'
nodes.rationale: The validation document's practical conclusion was right but the cause was wrong: ADR-0044 merged news_portal into blog_content, features intact, owner changed. src/modules/index.ts holds 20 modules and no news_portal; README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md (says 20, lists 21) and PROJECT_STATE.md (21 modules, 43 ADR, MODULE_CONTRACT_VERSION 2.3.0) were the stale part. Rule going forward: src/modules/index.ts is the strongest evidence, prose follows.
nodes.norm_label: correction 1 — news_portal was merged, not 'not yet built'

nodes.label: Correction 2 — cookie sessions already exist; the gap is cross-origin introspection
nodes.rationale: Half of the validation claim was true (auth/me is bearer-only) and the false half changed the design: login already sets httpOnly cookies and resolveAuthInputs accepts header OR cookie. The narrower, real gap is a session introspection contract for a different origin, called by the BFF.
nodes.norm_label: correction 2 — cookie sessions already exist; the gap is cross-origin introspection

nodes.label: Correction 3 — ABAC_ATTRIBUTES is a CLOSED allow-list, so subject.merchantIds/resource.merchantId are impossible
nodes.rationale: Attributes outside the list are invalid at authoring time and deny at evaluation time. Adding per-product attribute pairs would turn a bounded allow-list into a list that grows on request, destroying the very property that makes it valuable. Merchant is therefore modelled as a business scope reusing the already-allow-listed resource.businessScopeId.
nodes.norm_label: correction 3 — abac_attributes is a closed allow-list, so subject.merchantids/resource.merchantid are impossible

nodes.label: Correction 4 — FORCE RLS can silently fail to separate TENANTS too
nodes.rationale: FORCE RLS does not apply to superusers, and several PaaS make the default Postgres user a superuser; if the runtime DATABASE_URL points there, tenant isolation is entirely gone while migrations stay green and health checks stay 200. Isolation verification must run as awcms_app and be part of the test suite, not an assumption.
nodes.norm_label: correction 4 — force rls can silently fail to separate tenants too

nodes.label: Correction 6 — awcms-astro has since moved to Bun (ADR-0015 there)
nodes.rationale: The validation document correctly rejected 'runtime follows Bun' for its own date (engines Node >= 22.12, npm >= 10.9), but that fact changed: packageManager bun@1.3.14, bun.lock, bun test, oven/bun image, setup-bun in CI. The derived conclusion ('keep Node/npm until a migration ADR exists') no longer holds because the ADR exists and was executed. The whole AWCMS family is Bun-only.
nodes.norm_label: correction 6 — awcms-astro has since moved to bun (adr-0015 there)

nodes.label: Three things the validation document got right that implementers forget
nodes.rationale: UI visibility is not a security control (hiding a menu does not close an endpoint); different namespaces must not spawn three implementations of one business rule; external providers are never called inside a database transaction (outbox + idempotency key).
nodes.norm_label: three things the validation document got right that implementers forget

nodes.label: Varnish edge cache layer (ADR-0042)
nodes.rationale: Answers repeated anonymous public requests without waking the application at all — unlike ETag/Last-Modified (saves bandwidth, DB load unchanged) and src/lib/redis/ (fewer queries, app hop still there). Enabling order matters: application side first (EDGE_CACHE_MODE/endpoint/token), then schedule the purge worker, only then put Varnish in front.

nodes.label: Edge cache modes off / auto / on
nodes.rationale: off is default and truly inert (no header, no query, no behaviour change); auto ramps TTL from 0 as request rate/latency crosses thresholds; on always advertises declared surface TTLs. Mode never changes WHAT may be cached, only HOW LONG.
nodes.norm_label: edge cache modes off / auto / on

nodes.label: PUBLIC_CACHE_SURFACES surface registry
nodes.rationale: One entry per cacheable public surface with an anchored pattern ([^/]+ not .*), TTL, requiresTenant, an allow-list of query params, and a mandatory rationale explaining why it is safe to share. Routes that resolve their own tenant must publish Astro.locals.edgeCacheTenantId or their response is simply not cached — never mis-tagged.

nodes.label: edge-cache:surfaces:check gate (probes 16 must-never-cache paths)
nodes.rationale: Rejects unanchored patterns, greedy wildcards, duplicate keys, empty rationale and bloated query allow-lists, and actively probes 16 paths that must never be cacheable. It already caught a real bug: /blog/{code}/search is three segments and therefore matched the blog-post pattern although docs claimed search was excluded. It also requires purge emission from every module that owns a surface.

nodes.label: Hierarchical purge key scopes (tenant / module / surface / resource)
nodes.rationale: Content modules call enqueueEdgeCachePurge(tx, tenantId, scopes, reason) inside the SAME content transaction (outbox pattern, ADR-0006); delivery is done by a leased worker with retry. Keys are restricted to [A-Za-z0-9:._-] when built AND re-validated in VCL, because the key goes into a regex and a '.*' would turn one invalidation into a full cache flush.
nodes.norm_label: hierarchical purge key scopes (tenant / module / surface / resource)

nodes.label: Purge wire protocol POST /__edge-cache-purge
nodes.rationale: Uses X-Edge-Purge-Token + X-Edge-Purge-Key over POST because the application cannot use the real BAN method — Bun does not send non-standard HTTP methods. VCL still accepts genuine BAN so operators keep curl -X BAN. A container token that differs from the application's silently 403s every purge while the site serves stale content and looks healthy, which is why security:readiness reports endpoint-without-token as CRITICAL.

nodes.label: Three bugs that only appeared when Varnish actually ran (staging 2026-07-25/26)
nodes.rationale: The layer passed review and bun run check and was still wrong in three places, all of which REPORTED SUCCESS while not working: literal spaces in the ban expression ((^| )key( |$) splits on whitespace -> 'Wrong number of arguments', handler still answers 200; the BAN method never being sent; and sql/068's purge-queue RLS policy using awcms.tenant_id while withTenant sets app.current_tenant_id, which made WITH CHECK NULL, rejected the INSERT and — because enqueue is awaited inside the content transaction without a guard — made blog publish fail with 500 as soon as caching was switched on (fixed by sql/070). Root cause: sendEdgeCachePurge had no test at all, and a fetchImpl mock cannot catch the wire-level class of bug.
nodes.norm_label: three bugs that only appeared when varnish actually ran (staging 2026-07-25/26)

nodes.label: Verify with X-Cache, never trust exit codes
nodes.rationale: The only valid acceptance test is: warm an object to X-Cache: HIT, send a purge, confirm the next request MISSes, then HITs again. Rejected ban expressions, unsent methods and wrong-GUC RLS policies all slip past looser checks.
nodes.norm_label: verify with x-cache, never trust exit codes

nodes.label: Edge cache: what is deliberately not wired yet
nodes.rationale: blog_content and theming do emit purges; media_library deliberately does NOT because it owns no declared surface, so a ban on m:media_library would match nothing while the queue reports success — ceremony that looks like coverage but is zero. Host-resolved discovery surfaces (robots/sitemap/feed) are the best candidate but serveDiscovery does not receive locals so a route cannot publish its tenant. Admin-UI purge is deliberately excluded; queue + worker only.
nodes.norm_label: edge cache: what is deliberately not wired yet

nodes.label: Two deployed awcms environments (production and staging) plus local dev
nodes.rationale: One Coolify app PER environment, never one app with two domains — sharing an app means sharing env vars, which is exactly how staging accidentally writes to production data. Both run on the same Docker host behind Traefik with letsencrypt TLS.
nodes.norm_label: two deployed awcms environments (production and staging) plus local dev

nodes.label: Same owner identifier across environments, never the same password
nodes.rationale: awcms_identities is unique on (tenant_id, login_identifier), so one address in three environments is three separate accounts with three password hashes. Sessions cannot cross either: the token is an opaque random value stored as a sha256 hash in the tenant-scoped awcms_sessions table. A documented correction: AUTH_JWT_SECRET does not exist in awcms and there is no JWT in the session path — believing otherwise makes an operator think rotating it separates sessions.
nodes.norm_label: same owner identifier across environments, never the same password

nodes.label: Why PUBLIC_DEFAULT_TENANT_* is pinned even though resolution works without it
nodes.rationale: The chain host -> PUBLIC_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID -> PUBLIC_DEFAULT_TENANT_CODE -> awcms_setup_state.tenant_id always has an answer, but unpinned it is hidden in a table row rather than declared, and it can change silently once a second tenant appears. Real consumers are seo_distribution (robots/sitemap/feed) and site_search.
nodes.norm_label: why public_default_tenant_* is pinned even though resolution works without it

nodes.label: Permission seed migrations never reach pre-existing tenants (production incident 2026-07-26)
nodes.rationale: Seed migrations only apply to tenants created afterwards, so landing a new module gives its permissions to nobody who already exists; the symptom is 403 ACCESS_DENIED on an 'already installed' module. Happened in production: the owner lost 18 permissions (comments, site_search, form_drafts) after migrations 062-070. Backfill via INSERT ... SELECT into awcms_role_permissions is a deployment step, and 'full access' must then be verified against ABAC denies, SoD rules and business-scope limits, not just RBAC 197/197.
nodes.norm_label: permission seed migrations never reach pre-existing tenants (production incident 2026-07-26)

nodes.label: Local development made row-for-row identical to production (2026-07-26)
nodes.rationale: Before this, dev was a silently different environment — schema stopped at migration 30 vs production 70, zero tenants, no .env, and the only LOGIN role was a superuser. The most expensive bug classes (RLS leaks and permission 403s) were precisely the ones impossible to reproduce there, because a superuser pierces RLS and an empty tenant has no permissions to get wrong. Deliberate remaining differences: AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE, TRUSTED_PROXY_ENABLED (spoofable X-Forwarded-For without a proxy) and EDGE_CACHE_MODE.
nodes.norm_label: local development made row-for-row identical to production (2026-07-26)

nodes.label: Role separation is not active until roles get LOGIN PASSWORD
nodes.rationale: sql/019 and sql/022 create awcms_app/awcms_worker/awcms_setup as NOLOGIN without passwords on purpose — a password is a secret and secrets do not belong in migration files. Green migrations therefore do NOT mean role separation is on; until ALTER ROLE ... LOGIN PASSWORD runs and DATABASE_URL points at awcms_app, the runtime is a superuser and FORCE RLS is inert. Migrations still run as the DDL-owning role, not awcms_setup, which only holds USAGE on schema public.
nodes.norm_label: role separation is not active until roles get login password

nodes.label: The 0 / 1 / 0 RLS isolation proof run as awcms_app
nodes.rationale: Correct configuration is not proof of working isolation. As awcms_app: no tenant context must return 0 rows (fail-closed), own tenant 1, foreign tenant 0. If the first number is not 0 the policy is inert and everything after it is meaningless — and the same query run as a superuser passes while proving nothing.
nodes.norm_label: the 0 / 1 / 0 rls isolation proof run as awcms_app

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL serves two conflicting roles once .env exists
nodes.rationale: Bun loads .env itself, so DB-gated suites switch on locally. Runtime wants least-privilege awcms_app; the integration harness needs a privileged role because it creates ephemeral databases and runs ALTER ROLE (with awcms_app it fails 42501, it does not skip). Override all three of DATABASE_URL/SETUP_DATABASE_URL/WORKER_DATABASE_URL when running tests — leaving SETUP_DATABASE_URL from .env makes the harness fail with 'Connection closed', a message that points nowhere near the cause. The two suites must not share one bun test process.
nodes.norm_label: database_url serves two conflicting roles once .env exists

nodes.label: Coolify/postgres images create POSTGRES_USER as a superuser
nodes.rationale: Bit staging on 2026-07-25 and is memorable because the failure is completely invisible: the most natural post-provisioning shape points runtime DATABASE_URL at that user, and a superuser bypasses RLS unconditionally even with FORCE. Migrations green, health 200, every endpoint working, tenant isolation entirely absent. Verify with SELECT rolname, rolcanlogin, rolsuper, rolbypassrls — all must be f/f. ADMIN_DATABASE_URL is read by no code and only misleads the next reader.
nodes.norm_label: coolify/postgres images create postgres_user as a superuser

nodes.label: Staging isolation rules (own DB, own secrets, outbound integrations OFF)
nodes.rationale: Staging shares a host with production, so only configuration separates them and that configuration must be emphatic: own database/role/password, own secrets (copying production secrets means staging tokens work in production), R2_ENABLED=false, EMAIL_ENABLED=false, sync off. NEWS_PORTAL_PROFILE must be REMOVED rather than set to another value when staging has no R2, because full_online_r2 is the only accepted value and config:validate rejects it before deploy — a real mistake caught in awcms-micro.
nodes.norm_label: staging isolation rules (own db, own secrets, outbound integrations off)

nodes.label: Edge cache rollout: staging mode on, production mode auto
nodes.rationale: Staging uses on to PROVE the layer; production uses auto so nothing is cached while the origin is idle and TTL ramps only under load (>=5 req/s over a 60s window or >=250 ms mean origin latency; latch holds 3 windows). Varnish is a plain compose container, not a Coolify resource, and default.vcl is copied byte-for-byte from infra/varnish/default.vcl with a matching checksum so the reviewed file is the running file. Purge tokens differ per environment; the purge worker runs as a one-shot container from host cron because Dockerfile.production ships no scripts/.
nodes.norm_label: edge cache rollout: staging mode on, production mode auto

nodes.label: Production cache routing by Traefik priority, not by blanking the app FQDN
nodes.rationale: Staging moved its domain by clearing the app FQDN; production must not, because that means a redeploy and the Varnish backend disappears during it. Giving the Varnish router priority=100 makes cache selection deterministic (otherwise both routers tie and some traffic silently bypasses the cache) while leaving the app router as a fallback — proven useful: public requests kept being served directly during Varnish container recreation, zero downtime.
nodes.norm_label: production cache routing by traefik priority, not by blanking the app fqdn

nodes.label: Run migrations as a one-shot container, not docker exec
nodes.rationale: Dockerfile.production produces a runtime-only image without scripts/, so docker exec <app> bun run db:migrate fails with Module not found — that is the shape of the image, not a misconfiguration. Run from a repo checkout sharing the DB container's network namespace so the DSN is 127.0.0.1. Related sandbox trap: host->published-port TCP connects but the startup message is never answered ('Connection timeout after 30s'), easily misread as bad credentials. The oven/bun image has neither curl nor git.
nodes.norm_label: run migrations as a one-shot container, not docker exec

nodes.label: APP_URL is load-bearing for OIDC callbacks
nodes.rationale: Required by scripts/validate-env.ts and used by src/lib/auth/sso-config.ts to build the OIDC callback URL — a wrong host breaks login with redirect_uri_mismatch, not just an ugly link. Both redirect URIs must be registered at the IdP before staging is used for login.
nodes.norm_label: app_url is load-bearing for oidc callbacks

nodes.label: Tenant subdomain root domain is an explicitly-written assumption, not a decision
nodes.rationale: tenant-domain:dns:sync turns awcms_tenant_domains rows into real DNS records but needs a platform root domain the repo owner has not fixed. Choosing the wrong root is not a security hole (the adapter rejects hostnames outside the configured root) but a painful hostname migration later. Staging should stay on provider manual — two environments writing the same zone overwrite each other's serving records.
nodes.norm_label: tenant subdomain root domain is an explicitly-written assumption, not a decision

nodes.label: docs/awcms/repo-inventory.md — target-structure document whose body is stale
nodes.rationale: Marked GENERATED FILE but the generator (scripts/repo-inventory-generate.ts, bun run repo:inventory:generate) is not implemented/ported yet, so the body still says 'no modules' and 'no migrations' while the repo has 20 modules and 79 migrations. Deliberately carries no generation timestamp so a regeneration with no meaningful change does not diff; it always describes the commit it was committed at.
nodes.norm_label: docs/awcms/repo-inventory.md — target-structure document whose body is stale

nodes.label: Candidate RLS-exempt allow-list (infra/registry tables only)
nodes.rationale: Only global infra/registry tables qualify — awcms_schema_migrations (migration bookkeeping), awcms_tenants (the root registry other tables reference), awcms_permissions (global catalog), awcms_modules (global module catalog). No ERP business table (journal, stock movement, payroll run) may ever be exempt.

nodes.label: Stale negative claims inside a 'generated' inventory document
nodes.rationale: The file simultaneously claims 20 modules / 79 migrations in its status banner and 'no tables yet', 'no test files yet', '45 migration files' in its body — a generated-looking document that was never generated is trusted more than prose while being wrong.
nodes.norm_label: stale negative claims inside a 'generated' inventory document

nodes.label: Generated script inventory (60 targets, 23 in the check chain)
nodes.rationale: Generated from package.json by scripts:inventory:generate and enforced stale-free by scripts:inventory:check inside the check chain.
nodes.norm_label: generated script inventory (60 targets, 23 in the check chain)

nodes.label: Negative claims are the dangerous kind of documentation rot
nodes.rationale: The hand-written predecessor listed 12 of 52 scripts as active and called fifteen tools 'not yet ported' when all had landed, some already inside bun run check. 'X does not exist yet' gets more wrong over time and never fails by itself, unlike a positive claim which breaks the moment the code changes — a reader concludes db:work-class:check still needs building and builds a duplicate.
nodes.norm_label: negative claims are the dangerous kind of documentation rot

nodes.label: What stays out of bun run check, and why
nodes.rationale: The chain must be safe to run on any local checkout without a database, server, or PR context. Excluded: security:readiness (needs a migrated DB to inspect FORCE RLS, non-superuser app role, worker/setup grants), config:validate (needs a real environment), db/redis/email health, all scheduled workers, changesets:policy:check (PR-diff shaped), release:verify (only meaningful on a vX.Y.Z tag), and every *:generate whose *:check is the actual gate. The authoritative chain order lives in package.json and is deliberately not duplicated here to avoid drift.
nodes.norm_label: what stays out of bun run check, and why

nodes.label: Job schedules live in ModuleDescriptor.jobs, not in this README
nodes.rationale: Each module declares purpose, recommendedSchedule, environmentNotes and safeInOfflineLan; served via GET /api/v1/modules/{moduleKey}/jobs and gated by modules:jobs:check.
nodes.norm_label: job schedules live in moduledescriptor.jobs, not in this readme

nodes.label: Deferred reference scripts, guarded against silent resurrection
nodes.rationale: repo:inventory:generate/:check, config:docs:check, i18n:extract/:pot:check/:parity:check, database:capacity:check, production:preflight, resilience:dr-drill and performance:* are listed with their missing prerequisites — and scripts:inventory:check FAILS if any of those names ever appears in package.json, which is exactly how the previous table rotted.
nodes.norm_label: deferred reference scripts, guarded against silent resurrection

nodes.label: AWCMS Public API bundled OpenAPI contract (generated)
nodes.rationale: Generated by bun run openapi:bundle (scripts/openapi-bundle.ts, Issue #182) from openapi/awcms-public-api.src.yaml plus every openapi/modules/*.openapi.yaml fragment. Direct edits are silently overwritten and never reviewed as source of truth. OpenAPI 3.1.0, info.version 0.1.0.
nodes.norm_label: awcms public api bundled openapi contract (generated)

nodes.label: Security schemes bearerAuth / tenantHeader / syncHmac
nodes.rationale: bearerAuth is an opaque session token from POST /auth/login; tenantHeader (X-AWCMS-Tenant-ID) carries active tenant context; syncHmac is HMAC-SHA256 over '<timestamp>.<body>' with X-AWCMS-Node-ID/X-AWCMS-Timestamp for machine-to-machine sync. Every operation states its requirement explicitly — public operations are held in an ALLOWED_PUBLIC_OPERATIONS allow-list enforced by api:spec:check, so there is no implicit unauthenticated endpoint.

nodes.label: Root tag catalog (module-level API surface grouping)
nodes.rationale: Foundation, Tenant Admin, Identity & Access, Profile Identity, Logging & Audit, Module Management, Sync Storage, Workflow Approval, Email, Management Reporting, Reporting Projections, Domain Event Runtime, Theming, News Media, News Portal Homepage Sections, News Portal Ad Placements, SEO & Distribution, Form Drafts, Site Search, Comments. The tag descriptions carry the security invariants (a projection is never an authorization source; the search index is never an authorization source; comment submit responses are deliberately uniform so the endpoint is not an oracle).
nodes.norm_label: root tag catalog (module-level api surface grouping)

nodes.label: Application-level 128 KiB request body cap independent of the reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: Enforced in the application so it holds regardless of proxy configuration; an over-limit body returns 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE in the same envelope as every other error.
nodes.norm_label: application-level 128 kib request body cap independent of the reverse proxy

nodes.label: Blog Content OpenAPI module fragment
nodes.rationale: Owns every /api/v1/blog/* admin path and the schemas referenced only by this tag. The anonymous /blog/{tenantCode}/... family is deliberately NOT here — same convention theming's public preview routes use, since Astro text/html/xml routes under src/pages/** sit outside the api-spec-check route tree. Not independently valid OpenAPI: shared-component $refs resolve only after openapi:bundle merges it.

nodes.label: BlogContentBlock / BlogContentJson schemas (gated content-block vocabulary)
nodes.rationale: Publishes the whitelist content-block vocabulary as a gated contract instead of leaving content_json opaque to the API.

nodes.label: News Portal OpenAPI module fragment (homepage sections + ad placements)
nodes.rationale: One file per MODULE (Issue #182 convention): owns every path carrying the two News Portal tags. ADR-0036 already moved the presigned media surface (/api/v1/media/news-images/*) out to the media-library fragment. Port drops: the host-resolved /news/** public route family and the .astro admin pages were not ported, so this fragment is the admin HTTP surface only.
nodes.norm_label: news portal openapi module fragment (homepage sections + ad placements)

nodes.label: HomepageSection schemas (config validated per sectionType, sectionType immutable)
nodes.rationale: Every referenced post/category/media object must already exist for the same tenant, and gallery_block media must be a verified R2 object; sectionType cannot change after creation, while reordering is just a patchable sortOrder.
nodes.norm_label: homepagesection schemas (config validated per sectiontype, sectiontype immutable)

nodes.label: AdPlacement schemas (R2-only media reference)
nodes.rationale: mediaObjectId must reference a verified R2 media object of the same tenant — never a local path or arbitrary external image URL; linkUrl may be external but is validated server-side as an absolute http(s) URL only.

nodes.label: AWCMS API & Event Reference (generated from the bundled contracts)
nodes.rationale: Produced by bun run api:docs:generate from the bundled OpenAPI + AsyncAPI; api:docs:check (inside bun run check) fails the build when stale. Deliberately has no interactive version switcher and no external assets: it is generated 1:1 from the contracts at the same commit/tag, so reading a prior release means checking out that tag, and the file stays usable offline/LAN with any text editor.
nodes.norm_label: awcms api & event reference (generated from the bundled contracts)

nodes.label: Cross-cutting API conventions (envelope, pagination, idempotency, correlation)
nodes.rationale: Standard success envelope {data, meta} and error envelope with code/message/correlationId, keyset pagination, idempotency keys, correlation/request IDs and standard parameters are documented once for every module rather than repeated per operation.
nodes.norm_label: cross-cutting api conventions (envelope, pagination, idempotency, correlation)

nodes.label: Shared DomainEvent envelope and 44 documented channels
nodes.rationale: Every channel carries the same DomainEventEnvelope and producer direction is always send — there is no consumer/subscriber contract in this file. Message headers are HMAC-signed with the same scheme as Sync Storage requests.
nodes.norm_label: shared domainevent envelope and 44 documented channels

nodes.label: blog_content module (epic #536, first domain module registered directly in the base)
nodes.rationale: Owns posts, pages, taxonomies, revisions, settings, presentation extensions (templates/menus/widgets/ads/theme override), both public route families, and — after ADR-0044 — the absorbed news_portal homepage composer and R2-only ad placements. status is active, 39 permissions declared in module.ts.
nodes.norm_label: blog_content module (epic #536, first domain module registered directly in the base)

nodes.label: Two public route families: /news (default) and /blog/{tenantCode} (legacy)
nodes.rationale: Both always exist in every build; which one is used is a CONFIG choice (PUBLIC_TENANT_RESOLUTION_MODE), not a code choice. Neither redirects to the other and there is no plan to retire the legacy family (ADR-0010). The only real difference is tenant resolution: path segment via resolvePublicTenantByCode vs Host/domain lookup via resolvePublicTenantFromRequest. The legacy family suits offline/LAN deployments with no public domain at all.

nodes.label: withNewsTenant — shared tenant resolution + module-disabled + route-mode gate
nodes.rationale: Centralises everything the seven /news routes need before touching a post row. Uses fetchTenantModuleEntry (the single-module narrowing added as a security-audit follow-up so this anonymous gate reads only blog_content's row, not every registered module's) and fetchEffectivePublicRouteSettings. Every failure — unresolved tenant, disabled module, publicRouteMode disabled, no matching post — collapses to the same null/404, indistinguishable from the caller's side.
nodes.norm_label: withnewstenant — shared tenant resolution + module-disabled + route-mode gate

nodes.label: padUnresolvedTenantLatency — timing side-channel fix for host-based tenant probing
nodes.rationale: 'Tenant not resolved' and 'tenant resolved but blog_content disabled' both returned 404 but cost a different number of DB round trips, so an external prober varying the Host header could learn that a hostname maps to a real active tenant purely from latency once real domain mappings existed. The not-resolved branch now pays the same round-trip shape via a harmless padding query scoped to the all-zero fail-closed sentinel tenant id. Issue #564 extended the gate without reopening it by factoring both branches into ONE checkBlogContentAndRouteGate function so they cannot drift.
nodes.norm_label: padunresolvedtenantlatency — timing side-channel fix for host-based tenant probing

nodes.label: Two public visibility predicates (listing strict, detail allows unlisted)
nodes.rationale: The base rule and the extra listing rule are redundant unless the base rule is listing-only, so detail uses visibility IN ('public','unlisted') — which is the entire point of a tier between public and private. Acceptance criteria confirm the reading: unlisted is excluded from listing/search/feed/sitemap, not from all public access. Both live in public-blog-directory.ts so a maintainer who disagrees changes one place, not seven route handlers.
nodes.norm_label: two public visibility predicates (listing strict, detail allows unlisted)

nodes.label: content_json block schema + whitelist renderer
nodes.rationale: renderContentJsonToHtml only ever emits text through escapeHtml and there is no raw-html block type; unknown types or invalid fields are skipped silently rather than thrown. Adding image/embed/table means adding a case to the switch, never opening a raw-HTML escape hatch. Gallery items render only /

nodes.label: Author-own-draft ABAC override (evaluateContentUpdateAccess)
nodes.rationale: One permission must satisfy two requirements, so access is role permission OR (caller is authorTenantUserId AND status != published). Deliberately NOT placed in identity-access's evaluateAccess, which is the deny-biased cross-module evaluator (ADR-0004 default deny, deny overrides allow) — an ownership-based ALLOW override is blog_content business logic layered on top of evaluateAccess (called first, ownership consulted only when the sole deny reason is default_deny), not a new cross-module primitive. publish/schedule/archive/restore/purge have no ownership override at all.

nodes.label: Append-only revisions; restore adds a row, never overwrites
nodes.rationale: awcms_blog_revisions is never UPDATEd (same pattern as awcms_workflow_decisions/awcms_audit_events); restoring writes the old content back through the normal update path and then records a NEW revision, so intermediate revisions stay readable. revisions.restore is explicitly required with no ownership override, and Idempotency-Key replay returns the stored response without creating a second revision. Only significant changes (title/contentJson/contentText) create a revision — which is why the table has no slug column.
nodes.norm_label: append-only revisions; restore adds a row, never overwrites

nodes.label: Content quality checklist gate on publish/schedule
nodes.rationale: Runs server-side before the status transition, not only as a client preview; a no-op (applicable:false) unless full-online R2-only mode is active for the calling tenant. A blocking failure yields 422 CONTENT_QUALITY_CHECKLIST_BLOCKED plus a *_blocked_by_checklist audit event.
nodes.norm_label: content quality checklist gate on publish/schedule

nodes.label: Scheduled publishing worker restructured to SELECT ... FOR UPDATE + per-post gate
nodes.rationale: A single set-based UPDATE would let a tenant bypass the checklist entirely by scheduling a post BEFORE enabling R2-only mode and waiting for it to fall due — the same bypass class as the revision-restore hole. Now each due post is evaluated and a blocked one is LEFT scheduled (not silently published, not unscheduled) with a scheduled_publish_blocked audit; FOR UPDATE keeps two concurrent workers safe. Idempotent by construction, and COALESCE(published_at, now()) preserves an original publish timestamp.
nodes.norm_label: scheduled publishing worker restructured to select ... for update + per-post gate

nodes.label: Effective public route settings merged from two existing stores, not a third
nodes.rationale: publicRouteMode/publicBasePath/legacyTenantRouteEnabled/publicLabel come from the generic module-settings framework, while rssEnabled/sitemapEnabled deliberately stay in awcms_blog_settings. Duplicating those two into module settings would create two disconnected sources of truth — an admin could turn RSS off in the generic panel while the feed route keeps reading the old value. An integration test PATCHes the key into the WRONG store and proves the feed stays enabled, then flips the right store and proves it disables.
nodes.norm_label: effective public route settings merged from two existing stores, not a third

nodes.label: publicBasePath changes generated URLs only, not physical Astro routing
nodes.rationale: Astro cannot repoint a static file route's served path per tenant at runtime without a catch-all dynamic segment — a much larger, riskier restructuring out of scope. Consequence, documented rather than silently broken: a non-/news value produces self-referential links at a prefix Astro does not serve, and such a tenant must configure their reverse proxy/CDN accordingly.
nodes.norm_label: publicbasepath changes generated urls only, not physical astro routing

nodes.label: legacyTenantRouteEnabled disables with 404, never redirects
nodes.rationale: Three reasons: consistency with every other 'feature off' outcome in the module, which always collapses to the same generic 404; a redirect to /news would implicitly assert the tenant is also reachable by host resolution, which need not be true since the families resolve tenants independently; and a redirect target can itself leak information whereas the generic-404 convention trivially satisfies the do-not-expose-the-reason requirement. Deliberately gets no timing-parity treatment because tenantCode is caller-supplied and visible in the URL, so there is no existence question left to protect.

nodes.label: Two coexisting ad systems (free-URL awcms_blog_ads vs R2-only placements)
nodes.rationale: awcms_blog_ads.image_url accepts any http(s) URL — exactly the unmanaged-media hole media_library enforcement (ADR-0036) exists to close — while awcms_news_portal_ad_placements holds a real FK to a verified media object. Two systems for one feature is a temporary state, not a design: ADR-0044 §4 decided to unify them onto the verified-media table only AFTER widening it with the post/page targeting only the old system had, so unification does not silently delete capability. Until then, no new consumers of awcms_blog_ads.
nodes.norm_label: two coexisting ad systems (free-url awcms_blog_ads vs r2-only placements)

nodes.label: Absorption of news_portal into blog_content (ADR-0044)
nodes.rationale: What merged is OWNERSHIP, not shape: table names and API paths were deliberately left unchanged, following the ADR-0036 precedent that moved the media registry without renaming awcms_news_media_objects. Four permissions were repointed by sql/076 in insert -> repoint grant -> delete order so no tenant loses capability. awcms_news_portal_tenant_state was dropped (sql/077) because its only writer was never ported, leaving a FORCE-RLS table with no owner and no writer that every inventory gate would report as guarded by nobody. capabilities.consumes for media_library changed from optional to REQUIRED because ad placements hold a real FK to verified media — absorbing the code means absorbing its constraint.

nodes.label: /admin/blog SSR admin UI (Astro + vanilla JS, no new framework)
nodes.rationale: SSR reads through the same application-layer functions the JSON endpoints use; every mutation goes through the already-guarded/audited/idempotency-keyed /api/v1/blog/* endpoints — an admin page never writes to the database directly or bypasses the endpoint ABAC guard. Permission gating per section is defense-in-depth; real enforcement stays server-side. Categories and tags are two separate files precisely so 'tags cannot have a parent' is enforced structurally in markup — tags.astro never renders a parentId control at all, rather than hiding it conditionally.
nodes.norm_label: /admin/blog ssr admin ui (astro + vanilla js, no new framework)

nodes.label: 26 AsyncAPI channels whose real producer is the structured logger
nodes.rationale: Contract documentation only — there is no pub/sub dispatcher in this repo; the actual producer is src/lib/logging/logger.ts's log(). checkModuleEventChannels validates only module.ts -> AsyncAPI (every publishes entry needs a channel), not the reverse, which is why a channel with no producer (settings.updated) could sit unnoticed until Issue #543 added one.
nodes.norm_label: 26 asyncapi channels whose real producer is the structured logger

nodes.label: Explicit blog_content backlog (documented gaps, not oversights)
nodes.rationale: No public rendering for static pages, no page revision list/detail/restore routes (rows are written but unreachable), no page lifecycle endpoints despite seeded permissions — a caution that permission existence must not be read as feature existence — no public widget/ads rendering routes, no optimistic-concurrency check reading the incremented version column, no ts_rank relevance or per-locale text search config, no Accept-Language negotiation, and no robots.txt referencing the sitemap.
nodes.norm_label: explicit blog_content backlog (documented gaps, not oversights)

nodes.label: Known gap: /blog/{tenantCode} has no module-disabled check
nodes.rationale: A tenant that disables blog_content via the tenant-module API can still be browsed publicly through the legacy family; flagged deliberately as a follow-up (reuse withNewsTenant's pattern or extract a shared withTenantModuleGate) rather than retrofitted out of scope.
nodes.norm_label: known gap: /blog/{tenantcode} has no module-disabled check

nodes.label: Public offset pagination clamped at both ends (parsePageParam/boundedPageNumber)
nodes.rationale: These routes are public and unauthenticated, so ?page=1e8 used to become OFFSET 1e9 (Postgres scans and discards a billion rows while holding a pool connection — a one-request DoS) and ?page=abc became OFFSET NaN -> 500. Junk now normalises to page 1 rather than 400, because a broken ?page= on an HTML archive route should render the first page, not an error that gets indexed by crawlers; the clamped value is also what renders the pagination nav so ?page=abc never emits a NaN link.
nodes.norm_label: public offset pagination clamped at both ends (parsepageparam/boundedpagenumber)

nodes.label: Public routes written as .ts APIRoute rather than .astro pages
nodes.rationale: The repo has no test convention for .astro output — every integration test invokes APIRoute handlers directly through the harness — so writing these as .astro would have made them untestable by the established pattern while the issue explicitly demanded real end-to-end coverage of visibility leakage, SEO rendering and feed/sitemap filtering. invokeRaw() was added for non-JSON bodies since invoke() always JSON.parses.
nodes.norm_label: public routes written as .ts apiroute rather than .astro pages

nodes.label: Public error handling never leaks stack traces or tenant existence
nodes.rationale: Each handler is wrapped top-level: the real error is logged for operators while the client always receives a fixed generic HTML/XML string. A tenantCode that does not exist and one that is not active produce identical 404s (ADR-0009: do not leak tenant existence), and the same convention covers rssEnabled/sitemapEnabled being off.
nodes.norm_label: public error handling never leaks stack traces or tenant existence

nodes.label: Correction 7 — 'hybrid application' is not a valid Astro term
nodes.rationale: output is only static or server; mixed capability comes from export const prerender = false per route after an adapter is installed. The family-wide term adopted instead is 'static-by-default with on-demand routes'.
nodes.norm_label: correction 7 — 'hybrid application' is not a valid astro term

nodes.label: Language and content rules (i18n catalog, claims register)
nodes.rationale: UI strings go through the i18n catalog with Indonesian as the product's primary locale, never literals in components; numbers, currency and dates are formatted through i18n helpers and never string-concatenated; marketing claims, prices and service promises need an evidence owner and approval recorded in the claims register before going live.
nodes.norm_label: language and content rules (i18n catalog, claims register)
